observations: Photo 0 shows a white/pink industrial-style electric sewing machine with a large stitch selector dial and a vertical needle area.
Photo 1 shows a white sewing machine with visible brand text “SINGER” on the top front area and “Senco” and “Indigo 6” on the right side; there is also a stitch/setting dial.
Photo 2 shows a white sewing machine with “NOVAMATIC” and model text “NM 868A” on the front right; there is a stitch selection panel with multiple stitch icons and a speed/needle control dial.

claims.claim: Industrial electric sewing machine is use for sewing of clothes
claims.evidence: Photos show a powered sewing machine with standard needle/foot assembly suitable for garment sewing (photo 0/1/2).
Photos show multiple stitch options/icons (photo 2), but the exact supported functions (e.g., buttonhole, zigzag, heavy fabric capability) and accessories are not shown.

risks.risk: Whether the machine is fully working (motor, needle timing, feed, and speed control). Photos cannot confirm operation.
risks.proof: A short video of it sewing a straight line on fabric (including changing stitches) plus a close-up of the needle moving while running.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not guaranteed working (worst case: needs service/repair).

risks.risk: Whether it can handle heavy/industrial fabrics (thickness, feed strength, tension).
risks.proof: Video sewing through a thick fabric sample (e.g., denim or multiple layers) showing consistent feeding without skipping stitches.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as suitable for light-to-medium garment sewing only.

risks.risk: Missing/incorrect accessories (presser feet, bobbins, needles, power cord, manual). Photos don’t show what’s included.
risks.proof: Photo list of included items laid out (feet, bobbins, needles, power cable, any attachments) and a close-up of the bobbin case area.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as incomplete/unknown accessories (worst case: buyer may need to buy missing parts).

risks.risk: Brand/model confusion: photos show “SINGER” and “Indigo 6” text in photo 1, while photo 2 shows “NOVAMATIC NM 868A”. This could indicate mislabeling or a different unit.
risks.proof: Clear photo of the full model/serial plate (or sticker) on the machine body and the back/bottom label.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at the lowest confidence identity (worst case: treat as generic used sewing machine, not a specific NM 868A).

proof_requests: Send a clear close-up photo of the model/serial plate (and any sticker) on the machine body (not just front panel text).
Send a short running video: power on, needle moving, and sewing a straight stitch on fabric.
Show included accessories: presser feet, bobbins, needles, power cable, and any stitch/attachment tools.
Show a test on thicker fabric (e.g., denim) to confirm real capability.
response.reason: The photos identify a sewing machine and show multiple stitch controls, but the key pricing drivers (confirmed working condition, included accessories, and whether the correct model is NM 868A vs possible mislabeling) are not provable from photos alone.
